What is Custom Pork and Beef?

We offer whole, half and for beef quarter options of buying an animal. What does that mean? Essentially you are buying a whole or a half share or quarter share of an animal. That means all the meat you receive comes from the same animal. Once the animal arrives at the butcher it is yours and the butcher is following your specific instructions on how to cut your animal up into any kind of cuts and smoked products you'd like. With that being said there is only so many ribeyes for example on an animal so if requested you will only get as many ribeyes as there are on a beef. Half and quarter shares simply divide that number in half and a quarter respectively.

How much does it cost?

The final price of your meat depends on the size of your animal. You will need to pay for the meat, the processing (butcher's fee), and delivery if you choose this option. We charge by the hanging weight, which is the weight of the animal once it's been skinned or scrapped and organs removed. Our beef on average hangs at 600 lbs and pork at 200 lbs. For a half it will be the weight divided by 2, and a quarter is the full hanging weight divided by 4. Our prices are as follows: whole beef $5.75/lb, half beef $5.85/lb, quarter beef $6.00/lb, whole pig $4.25/lb, half pig $4.50/lb.

The butcher will also have a fee to cut the meat. This amount depends on the type of cuts that you get. Typically, sausages and smoked meats will raise your final price. The average cost of processing for a whole beef is $650. The average cost of a whole pig is $335.

Finally, we charge $25 to have your bulk meat delivered to your home. Picking up from the butcher or from our farm in Spring Green is free.

How much meat will I receive?

Expect that the amount of meat you get will be less than the hanging weight of the animal. This is because excess bone and fat is removed from the animal during the processing. Generally you can expect 65-70% of the hanging weight for a beef and 70-75% for a pig.

What cuts can I get?

Weber Meats has great information on their website about how many of each cut you can expect from an animal.

From Our Family to Yours

Seven Seeds Farm is an 8 generation farm with 4 generations currently living and working on the farm. The farm was originally a dairy until tough times and low milk prices led to a shift to conventional row-cropping.

Greg and Lea took over the farm in 2006, wanting to raise food that was healthy, safe and really tasty. Over the years it went from a hobby farm to feed the family to raising beef, pork and chicken for all over Southwest Wisconsin. The same principles still ring true: if we wouldn't eat it, we wouldn't raise it.

We don't think labels are the most important thing, but we want to reassure our customers that we practice what we preach. That's why we are certified organic, certified 100% grass-fed, and Animal Welfare Approved.

As a multi-generational farm, keeping our land healthy is important too. We are a regenerative farm, meaning we are actually growing soil and reducing carbon in the atmosphere with our farming methods. At the rate the majority of farms are going, there will be no soil, no drinkable water, and devastating change in weather patterns unless we make changes today. We use methods like intensive, rotational grazing, cover crops, and silvopasture (trees within the pasture) to reduce erosion, build soils, and sequester carbon.
